subject: Prod readiness: tenancy & isolation follow-up (MedTech.AI)
body:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.m@redwood.com>
To: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@medtech.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Prod readiness: tenancy & isolation follow-up (MedTech.AI)

Sam — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on where Redwood can help as you plan for production: 

Call highlights (short):
- Primary concern: isolation/noisy-neighbor risk for latency-sensitive clinical inference workloads (MedTech.AI inference for triage)
- Traffic profile: steady baseline ~45 req/s with spiky 10x bursts during batch imports; median request size ~120 tokens, worst-case 1024 tokens
- Non-negotiables: P95 latency SLO <= 300ms for model endpoints used in clinician flows; strict audit/logging for PHI pathways

Redwood take (high level):
- Hosted API (shared infra): fastest onboarding, built-in prefix/KV caching; suitable if you accept soft SLOs and can tolerate noisy-neighbor risk during bursty windows with auto-fallback policies
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools): recommended if you need predictable throughput and strict P95 latency guarantees; we can pin model variants and dedicate GPU slices to your workload
- Private VPC/on-prem: best when security/compliance and network isolation must be customer-controlled; supports HSM/KMS integrations and audit export.

Action items I propose:
1) Technical deep-dive with your infra lead + our infra engineer (Neha) to go over sequence-length distributions, KV-cache strategy, and expected concurrency (target ~60–100 concurrent model calls).
2) Two-week Dedicated POC (small reserved pool) with canary routing from Hosted-to-Dedicated for production fallback testing.
3) Share SOC2 summary and deployment-options matrix (attached) for legal + security review.

Attached: redwood-deployment-options-matrix.xlsx (matrix + cost model), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

Thanks — Rafael

--
Rafael Mendes
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael.m@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0118

Sam — quick answers and a technical sketch below. I attached a short deployment-options matrix (same as Rafael referenced) and an ops checklist we use for POCs.

1) Noisy-neighbor evidence: in shared clusters we occasionally see P95 latency spikes tied to large batch jobs; typical magnitude: 200–600ms delta at P95 for 90s windows during noisy events. We mitigate with autoscaling and per-customer request queuing, but that does not eliminate variability.

2) Minimal GPU guidance: based on your baseline/burst profile, we recommend starting the Dedicated POC on 2x A10G-equivalent GPUs (or 1x A100/RTX6000-class depending on model size). This provides headroom for 10x bursts with continuous batching. We can produce a cost delta table vs shared.

3) Provisioning time: Dedicated pools in us-west typically provision in ~4–6 hours for standard configs; expedited in 1–2 hours if we reserve capacity in advance. For the POC we can pre-warm images to guarantee fast ramp.

Ops checklist (high level):
- KV-cache TTL and prefix caching keys defined
- Canary routing rule (10% traffic) + automated rollback on errors > 1% for 5m
- Observability: token-level latency, per-route P95, and cost per 1k tokens dashboards
- Audit logs: continuous export to your S3 (encrypted) + retention policy for 7 years (configurable)

Next step: Rafael / Neha — can we schedule the deep-dive tomorrow or Wednesday (window: 9–11 PST)?

Regards,
Monica

--
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference

Looping in some infra details from our side so your SREs have something concrete ahead of the deep-dive.

Key SLO/guardrails we enforce for Dedicated POCs:
- Target P95 latency: <= 300ms (measurements taken at edge before client-side network)
- CPU/GPU contention monitoring with automatic throttles for cross-tenant batch jobs
- KV cache warm-up period to observe hit-rate > 60% before full traffic cutover

Network/isolation notes:
- Dedicated pools provide tenant network namespaces + isolated init containers; for Private VPC we offer customer-managed subnets and peering with strict CIDR allowances
- Audit exports: signed, time-stamped event logs (JSONL) delivered to your bucket every 5 minutes; we can push to a 3rd-party SIEM if required

I'll bring the runtime engineer to the deep-dive to walk through kernel selection and sequence-length perf characteristics.

-Neha

Proposed next steps:
- Technical deep-dive: Wed 20 Jan, 10:00 PST (Neha + runtime engineer + your infra lead). I'll send a calendar invite after you confirm.
- Dedicated POC: 2-week run starting the week after the deep-dive. Canary config: 10% traffic for days 1–2, increase to 50% after KPIs met, then full switch if P95 and error targets hold for 48h.
- Acceptance criteria (POC): sustained P95 <= 300ms; error rate < 0.5%; cache hit-rate > 60% within 48 hours.
- Cost estimate: we'll provide a POC quote; ballpark for 2x A10G-equivalent for 2 weeks ~ $6k–$9k (depends on region & model quantization).

If that looks reasonable, Sam, can you confirm the deep-dive time and share the infra lead's email so we can include them? Also confirm Legal's preferred channel for SOC2 review (email or secure link).
